cf.title: Lost KEY SHARE lock information during toasting allows foreign-key violation

input.subject: lost lock during toasting allows fk violation

verdict_reasoning: The bug is real and the fix is wanted: message #1 shows an orphaned child row from ordinary DML. Two fixable design points survive at level 2. replication-ondisk-1 shows v1 writes a lock-only xmax naming the updater and a duplicate multixact member, and maintenance-fit-1 shows the recheck condition already missed one unlock path. Rui's follow-up patches address both, but no merged version exists and nobody has answered message #4.

brief.title: Keep foreign-key KEY SHARE locks taken while heap_update() does TOAST work
brief.problem: heap_update() releases the buffer lock for TOAST or page-extension work, and a KEY SHARE lock taken in that window by a foreign-key check is overwritten when the update stamps xmax. The referenced row can then be deleted without waiting, leaving an orphaned child row. The reporter reproduced it on master with plain large TOAST values, in 12 of 12 timed trials.
brief.proposed_design: v1 moves the computation of the old and new tuple xmax to after the TOAST and page-extension block, once the buffer lock is held again. If the xmax or t_infomask changed meanwhile, the patch assumes a concurrent locker and sets locker_remains. A reviewer's follow-up patches gate the recheck on the condition that released the buffer lock and keep the updater's temporary lock out of both tuples.
user_visible_surface: New injection point heap_update-toast-unlocked, plus an isolation test, in the reviewer's 0002.
author_claims: The bug is an ordering problem in heap_update(): xmax is computed before the TOAST step and written after it.
An isolation test that renames a TOAST table triggers the bug without a concurrent workload.
fk-toast-lock fails on master and passes with v1 (reviewer's report).
The reviewer says the orphan is still reachable with v1, through an update of an unrelated column when the toaster has nothing to do.
The reviewer says v1 leaves the new tuple locked by the updater itself and adds the updater to the multixact twice; their 0001 fixes both.
brief.thread_state: The reporter, Michael Paquier (two messages and v1) and reviewer Rui Zhao (0001 and 0002 on top of v1) took part; Peter Geoghegan and Alvaro were CC'd but did not reply. The CommitFest entry needs a rebase, and nobody has answered Rui's findings.
unclear: Which back branches have the bug; the reporter tested master only, and the target is stable.
Whether page extension without TOAST hits the same window, and whether a test covers it.
How the patch handles locker_remains and checked_lockers; Michael was unsure about this.
Whether v1 and the reviewer's patches will be merged into one version, and who rebases it.
The end of the reviewer's message, including part of point 3, is cut off.

objections.title: v1 persists wrong xmax and multixact state on disk and on standbys
objections.failure_scenario: A minor release ships v1. A plain update of a row with an external value stamps the new tuple with a lock-only key-share xmax naming the updater itself. Updates that meet a real key-share locker create multixacts holding the updater twice. Both forms are WAL-logged, replayed on standbys and kept through pg_upgrade, and nobody notices until the headers confuse a later lock check or pg_multixact members grow faster.
objections.argument: Message #4 shows the new tuple's xmax at the updater's own xid on v1, where master writes 0. It also shows an extra fornokeyupd member in both multixacts, and a caller's tuple whose header no longer matches the stored one. These headers live in heap pages and pg_multixact and pass to standbys through the update WAL record, so a stable-branch fix cannot take them back once released. Nobody has answered message #4, and message #3 says the locker_remains logic is unsettled.
objections.author_must_show: Which xmax and infomask invariants does the merged version keep on the old and new tuple, and does replay produce the same headers as the primary?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 shows v1 writing the updater's own xid as a lock-only xmax and a duplicate multixact member. Rui's 0001 restores the master output, but no merged version exists and nobody has answered, so this stays open as fixable.

objections.title: Recheck is tied to a proxy condition, so later unlock paths can skip it
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds another path in heap_update() that drops the buffer lock, or changes when the toaster returns its input tuple. The xmax recheck does not run on that path, and a concurrent KEY SHARE lock is lost again. Nothing fails until someone finds an orphaned child row in production.
objections.argument: Message #4 shows the v1 recheck already misses one unlock path. v1 gates on `heaptup != newtup || newbuf != buffer`, but the unlock happens under `need_toast || newtupsize > pagefree`. Rui's 0001 realigns the two conditions, yet the design still needs every future edit of this block to keep the conditions in step. Only an injection-point test for one path would fail loudly if they drift.
objections.author_must_show: Can the recheck be keyed on a single record that the buffer lock was released, so any new unlock path in heap_update() is covered without a separate change?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 shows the two conditions already drifted once inside v1. Rui's 0001 realigns them, but the material does not show that one record of the unlock drives the recheck, so the question is fair.

refuted.title: Stable-branch change to heap_update locking has no engaged heapam owner
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer back-patches a reordered xmax computation into every supported branch. A subtle multixact error like the ones message #4 found in v1 (the updater locking its own new tuple, a duplicate multixact member) ships in a minor release. Users see it only later, as wrong lock state or visibility problems after upgrading.
refuted.argument: The target is stable, but only master was tested (message #1). Michael called the code tricky and asked for more eyes (message #3), and he was unsure about locker_remains and checked_lockers (message #2). Peter G. and Alvaro were CC'd and did not reply, and nobody answered Rui's findings, which show that v1 changed tuple state even when no concurrent session was present. The fix is wanted, but nobody who owns this code has signed off on it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which branches have the bug, and will a committer who knows heapam and multixact locking review one merged version before it is back-patched?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1 for the failure scenario. The rest is committability: a committer wrote v1 and asked for more review, and missing sign-off on an unmerged patch is not a design flaw.

touch_points.reason: The patch changes which xmax and infomask values heap_update() stamps on heap tuples, and which multixact members it creates.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby

questions: Which xmax and infomask values does the merged version write on the old and new tuple, and does replay on a standby produce the same headers?
Can the recheck be keyed on one record that heap_update() released the buffer lock, so a new unlock path is covered without a separate change?
Which back branches have the bug, and does the same patch apply to each of them?
Does page extension without TOAST work open the same window, and does a test cover that path?
How should locker_remains and checked_lockers be set when the xmax changed while the buffer lock was released?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier wrote v1 and asked for more review; a committer who knows heapam tuple locking and multixacts should also confirm the merged version.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the tuple xmax and multixact state that heap_update() writes in every back-patched branch. Wrong headers persist in heap pages and on standbys after a minor release and cannot be taken back.
committability.author_follow_up: Michael posted v1 one day after the report and invited comments, but nobody has answered Rui's findings in message #4 and the entry needs a rebase.

priority.reason: Users of foreign keys whose referenced tables have TOASTed columns can get orphaned child rows from ordinary DML (message #1). The patch is small, but it changes tuple locking in heap_update() for stable branches, so review needs care and one merged, rebased version.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the handling of locker_remains and checked_lockers, the page-extension path and the exact headers written by the merged version could not be checked. The end of message #4 is cut off.

precedents_retrieved.title: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: When tuple_update() or tuple_delete() finds a concurrently updated tuple in read committed mode, the table AM locks the updated version itself instead of returning TM_Updated for a separate tuple_lock() call. Later versions also had update and delete return the old tuple through a slot passed by the executor, which avoids refetching it and helps table AMs with costly TID lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Version 15 was committed in March 2023, then reverted after Andres Freund's post-commit review. He showed that RETURNING could use the wrong tuple, with an isolation test that fails. He also criticised the new API: the ignored wait parameter, tmfd turned into an input, and the LazyTupleTableSlot code. The redesigned old-tuple API came days before the version 16 feature freeze, and he said it was not ready for 16. In March 2024 the author planned to push a revised version, and the visible messages do not show why the entry was finally returned with feedback in October 2024.

precedents_retrieved.title: POC: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes tuple_update() and tuple_delete() lock a concurrently updated tuple as soon as they detect it, so a separate tuple_lock() call before the read committed recheck is no longer needed. It also simplifies nodeModifyTable.c and removes an extra table_tuple_fetch_row_version() call in ExecUpdate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message, from the author on 2022-07-29, said a benchmark showed a small, noisy gain and that he would bring the patch into a more acceptable shape. No later message appears before the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: disallow HEAP_XMAX_COMMITTED and HEAP_XMAX_IS_LOCKED_ONLY
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch treats HEAP_XMAX_COMMITTED together with HEAP_XMAX_IS_LOCKED_ONLY as an invalid infomask combination, documents this in README.tuplock, and drops the code in heapam_visibility.c that handles it. It also adds amcheck reports for the combination, plus assertions in the visibility functions; erroring in non-assert builds was considered as an option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn. In the last exchange, Andres Freund questioned whether also disallowing the pre-v9.3 locked-only bit pattern was viable. Nathan Bossart replied that he saw no such case in the v9.2 code and asked whether to limit the check to the v9.3+ pattern; no reply follows. Earlier, Mark Dilger warned that a pattern no current code path creates may still have been written by a past release or upgrade path.

precedents_retrieved.title: heap_insert() and heap_update() optimization
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reduced repeated BufferGetPage(buffer) calls inside heap_insert() and heap_update() to make these functions faster. The author reported speedups of about 5.6% for heap_insert() and 11.4% for heap_update() in an optimized build.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author repeated the timing tests and found no real gain: the patched build averaged 1303 against 1272 for the original. He suggested that autovacuum, analyze or a checkpoint may have affected the first run. Andres Freund had said the first numbers looked large and suggested checking the generated code. The thread ends there, and the entry was rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forcing new tuples of updates off the page
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a table storage parameter, local_update_limit, that keeps an update from placing the new tuple on the old tuple's page when that page lies beyond a set size, so the tuple moves to an earlier page found through the FSM. Users could then shrink a bloated table through normal UPDATE traffic and vacuum truncation, without the exclusive locks of VACUUM FULL or CLUSTER.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas and Andres Freund objected that users have no good way to pick a fixed page limit. A limit set too low or left in place as the table grows causes pointless non-HOT updates and index bloat. Andres Freund proposed basing the decision on relation size against free space known to the FSM, and Laurenz Albe agreed and set the entry to waiting for author. The author withdrew the patch because he lacked the time and expertise for that rewrite.

precedents_retrieved.title: partial heap only tuples
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds partial heap only tuples (PHOT), so an update creates new index tuples only for indexes whose columns changed, and those index tuples point to the new heap tuple. Index scans follow a PHOT chain only while their own indexed columns stay unchanged, and pruning of PHOT chains is restricted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying to HEAD, and the entry was set to Waiting for Author in July 2021. No updated patch was posted, so the entry was returned with feedback in November 2021. The visible messages show design concerns, such as index create/drop handling and long-term heap fragmentation, but no objection that decided the outcome.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make VACUUM remove MultiXacts with updater XIDs more eagerly
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes FreezeMultiXactId() so that VACUUM removes a MultiXact outright when all of its members are older than OldestXmin, instead of leaving it in place with FRM_NOOP processing. The goal is to get more use out of each GetMultiXactIdMembers() call and to remove more Multis that have updater XIDs, since OldestMxact can be held back much longer than OldestXmin.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread ends when Peter Geoghegan creates the CF entry. No message shows a reviewer objecting to this patch or the author explaining the withdrawal. Andres Freund's objections in the thread concern the separate patch that skips the TransactionIdDidCommit() sanity checks.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow reads to proceed during FK/trigger drops by reducing relation-level lock from AccessExclusive to ShareRowExclusive
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lowers the relation-level lock taken while dropping foreign key constraints and their RI triggers from AccessExclusiveLock to ShareRowExclusiveLock, so that SELECTs on the other table keep running. A revised patch narrowed the change to RI action triggers on the referenced table and kept AccessExclusiveLock elsewhere.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the change is unsafe for FK removal, because the planner may have built query plans that rely on the constraint holding, as the comment in AlterTableGetLockLevel explains. He also noted that the first patch lowered the lock for other constraint types, and that dropping a unique constraint can also break existing plans. The author posted a narrower patch, but no one replied to it, and the visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The precedent search returned no row about the same or a similar idea, and the thread points to no earlier discussion of losing a KEY SHARE lock during the TOAST step of heap_update(). This is a bug fix, so a prior-rejection objection does not apply.

This is a bug fix inside heap_update() with no new syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump format or psql change, so the user-facing contract is untouched. Its intended visible effect is that a DELETE of a referenced row now waits or raises the foreign-key error, which is the documented behaviour. Rui's report in message #4 says v1 makes RETURNING xmax and pgrowlocks show the updated row locked by its own transaction. That is a visible change, but it is a correctness defect for the design and safety angles, and 0001 removes it.

The fix adds no WAL record type, catalog change or wire change. The concern is only the tuple header and multixact state that v1 writes, which persists and replicates. The page-extension path and back-branch scope could not be checked from the material.

The proposal adds no privilege, role, GUC or exposure: it reorders xmax computation inside heap_update(), and the new injection point exists only in builds with injection points enabled. The lost KEY SHARE lock is a data-integrity bug that any user with insert and delete rights can hit, but the remaining gaps (message #4) are correctness issues for other angles.

The fix is for silent foreign-key violations, so it is desirable. Its extra cost falls only on updates that leave the buffer unlocked for TOAST or page-extension work. The objections above concern long-run fragility and ownership. They are not reasons to reject the fix.

This is a data-integrity bug fix in heap_update(), where a KEY SHARE lock from a foreign-key check is lost during TOAST work. No existing feature, setting, documented idiom or extension prevents the orphaned child row, so from this angle the need is not already met.

No demand objection applies. This is a data-integrity bug fix: a foreign-key constraint can be violated with ordinary DML, and the report reproduces it in 12 of 12 timed trials without special setup (message #1). Every user of foreign keys on tables with TOASTed columns is exposed, and the fix adds no new user-facing feature or setting.
